description: Verify that DUT silently discards a UDP datagram with a non-zero invalid checksum (RFC 1122 §4.1.3.4 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 1122 §4.1.3.4 says receivers MUST silently discard UDP datagrams whose checksum is non-zero and does not verify. 'Silently' means no ICMP error, no log noise to the sender — the bad bits are dropped on the floor. (Checksum=0 is the legitimate 'no checksum' opt-out, covered by FIELDS_16.)

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram with a deliberately corrupted (non-zero) checksum

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram (UT-query confirms drop)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the bad-checksum UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered a UDP with invalid checksum (checksum verification disabled or bypassed)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently discarded the bad-checksum UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received UDP with invalid checksum
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for invalid-checksum discard
